diagnoses.localizedCause: Root cause is the reusable TaskTemplate log-analytics-pipeline@1 (digest f5af010854f8faf4c3c88bf90097e75798d8ace2c8d6d450191dd51648405e8f), not the coordinator and not the stage workers. Its decomposition.children are listed parse-log-events, render-stats-report, aggregate-event-stats — i.e. report BEFORE aggregate — and carry no dependency/ordering edge; the runtime 'starts the children one at a time in dependency order' (seq 24), which with zero edges degenerates to recipe list order. Observed timeline proves the mechanism: parse r-f51a7635 started 05:43:47.9 / finished 05:44:04.2; report r-071e165f started 05:44:04.2 and its freshness gate `test -f out/stats.json && …` exited 1 because out/stats.json did not yet exist (submission of r-071e165f, evidence-r-071e165f-a08e-4ff1-8159-08ae0bcfb3c5-81abbe3d-b4ae-49d5-ac53-c58037e23d31); aggregate r-0725f408 only wrote out/stats.json at 05:44:11–05:44:30, i.e. after the report window — the coordinator's own post-batch mtime evidence shows stats.json 13:44:20 vs events.json 13:43:59 (session s-9dd7e2ab seq 58). So render-stats-report's declared upstream input ('the verified out/stats.json produced by this run's upstream aggregation stage') is real but not encoded in the recipe. The pipeline contract itself forbids the coordinator from repairing this: it may not author stage contracts inline, must 'bind the parse, report and aggregate children in recipe order', and a failed stage ends the pipeline with no second batch — so the honest terminal failure with a gap report was the correct behaviour, and the defect must be repaired by the template's owner. Note the template's objective prose repeats the same wrong order ('parse, report and aggregate children in recipe order'), so a repair must fix both the children order (or add an explicit report-after-aggregate edge) and that wording, otherwise a re-expansion reproduces the failure. Next action for the business coordinator of the still-running parent t-3b768fcd-901f-42b2-8b26-98a316b862df: do NOT re-dispatch the failed report stage, do not admit a workaround batch, and do not retry t-13a8d7bc (its run r-686e325c is terminal/failed); escalate the defective template to its owner (evolution proposal on template id log-analytics-pipeline) and, only after a repaired template version exists, decompose one fresh child bound to that repaired template so pipeline-result is re-verified end-to-end on a fresh checkout — a new attempt on a corrected contract, not a retry of the failed stage. import { readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs'
import { dirname } from 'node:path'

const stats = JSON.parse(readFileSync('out/stats.json', 'utf8'))
const { total, perLevel, errorRate } = stats

const lines = [
  '# Log Report',
  'Total: ' + total,
  'INFO: ' + perLevel.INFO,
  'WARN: ' + perLevel.WARN,
  'ERROR: ' + perLevel.ERROR,
  'Error rate: ' + errorRate,
]

mkdirSync(dirname('out/report.md'), { recursive: true })
writeFileSync('out/report.md', lines.join('\n') + '\n')
